title: SLO and tracing strategy for analytics ingestion and console backends
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a coherent SLO/SLI framework, tracing propagation conventions, and logging standards for the analytics ingestion pipeline and the Console backend services that surface usage metrics. Goal is to reduce time-to-detect/diagnose regressions in analytics, ensure actionable alerts, and provide clear dashboards for on-call and product stakeholders.
acceptance_criteria: SLI definitions documented for ingestion request latency, ingestion success rate, ingestion-to-store pipeline lag, and critical Console API endpoints
SLO targets and error budgets defined and approved by Product and SRE
Tracing context propagation implemented end-to-end across API -> ingestion workers -> ETL -> metrics store with at least 90% trace coverage for production traffic
Logging schema standardized for ingestion events (request_id, tenant_id, model, route, size_bytes, processing_time_ms) and indexed in log service
Dashboards created: ingestion health overview, per-tenant hotpaths, error budget burn, and high-cardinality troubleshooting view
Alerting rules published with runbooks and onboarding notes in Confluence
tasks: Workshop with Product/SRE to align on high-level SLOs (P0 list)
Draft SLI definitions and measurement queries (metrics, traces, logs)
Instrument trace headers and verify propagation across services and worker queues
Add structured logging fields to ingestion code paths and Console backend handlers
Create dashboards and templated per-tenant views in Grafana/Looker
Implement alert rules and integrate with PagerDuty and Slack runbook channels
Run a 2-week canary to validate alert thresholds and adjust based on noise
decisions: Adopt W3C Trace-Context for all distributed tracing headers to stay compatible with vendor and open-source tracers
Primary metric backend for SLIs will be Prometheus (pushgateway for short-lived workers) with aggregated traces in Jaeger/Tempo
Use structured JSON logging to ensure consistent schema for ingestion events; ingest into our ELK cluster with index mapping for tenant_id and request_id
SLOs will be tenant-scoped for high-usage customers and global for system-level SLA observability
Initial SLO targets: 99.9% successful ingestion for production tenants, 95th percentile end-to-end ingestion latency < 800ms under normal load

2025-02-25: Tracing headers added to API gateway and ingestion dispatcher; validated propagation across queued worker in staging using synthetic load
2025-03-01: Logging schema PR opened to add tenant_id and request_size fields to ingestion producer (PR: see links); early feedback from Observability team requested
2025-03-04: After SRE review, we tightened the 95th percentile latency SLO to 800ms and added an explicit SLO for KV cache miss cost spikes
